findings.title: Materials' 123% earnings bet is a mirage
findings.body: The market is pricing in a 123 percent earnings surge, yet the forward P/E sits at the 36th percentile while trailing sits at the 91st. This is a sector where analysts are betting on a massive re-rating, not a cyclical uptick. The 55 percent compression is the market's way of saying current earnings are the anomaly, not the future.

findings.title: Health Care's 86% growth is a red flag
findings.body: A 2-point percentile gap between forward and trailing valuations is remarkably tight, yet it masks an 86 percent implied earnings surge. The market is not rewarding this sector for its past; it's pricing in a future that looks increasingly like a one-off. This is a sector where the multiple is being held hostage by a single, aggressive assumption.

findings.title: Communication Services is a value trap at the 2nd percentile
findings.body: At the 2nd percentile, the forward P/E is as cheap as it gets, but the trailing multiple is at the 29th percentile, showing a 26-point gap. The market is not just pricing in a recovery; it's pricing in a 57 percent earnings explosion. This is a classic value trap where the market is saying the current earnings power is not the base case.
